description: I am an engineering mind who looks at the Moon and doesn't just see a pretty rock, I see a future real estate market with terrible lighting and zero Wi-Fi.
summary:
We developed Hecate, an interactive 3D planetary navigator and decision-support platform designed to identify, evaluate, and rank safe landing sites across the lunar South Pole on a full moon globe. 

To address the environmental challenges of lunar exploration, Hecate integrates NASA datasets including LOLA 5 meter elevation models, PGDA illumination and cold trap maps, and Mini-RF Radar ice indicators, as well as international partner datasets. The system performs real time multi-criteria evaluations that simultaneously analyze terrain landing hazards (slope, roughness, and vertical uncertainty) with operational survival requirements, simulating dynamic solar power generation and direct-to-earth communication sightlines across customizable mission timelines. 

This is critical because South Pole exploration demands an engineering trade-off which is accessing water ice inside permanently shadowed craters while avoiding hazardous slopes and surviving extreme eclipse periods. By implementing multiple archives into an automated search and quantitative site-by-site comparisons, it eliminates planning risks and delivers the validation needed for safe lunar site landings.
details:
HECATE is an interactive 3D web platform that evaluates and ranks candidate landing sites across the lunar South Pole (80°S–90°S) on a continuous full-Moon globe. It operates in two modes:

  • Forward Search: Automatically screens the South Polar region on a 4.75 km grid across custom launch windows, using background processing to calculate sunrise, sunset, and communication windows down to the second.
  • Site Analysis: Inspects any coordinate or 12 curated Artemis III/CLPS targets. It generates 360° terrain horizons out to 150km, calculates dynamic solar power generation, tracks Direct-to-Earth (DTE) visibility, and issues an instant feasibility verdict for future missions (PASS, FAIL, or LOW CONFIDENCE).

The platform works on the following tasks to deliver both educational value and long-term use for future exploration:

  • De-risking Artemis & CLPS Missions: Verifies landing stability, electrical power budgets, and communications for upcoming lunar surface missions.
  • Eliminating Planning Bias: Prevents fatal single-variable assumptions.

HECATE acts as an an optimized tool of evaluation for NASA Landing sites. Its specific features include:

  • Built-in Education & Step-by-Step Tutorial: Includes an interactive guided walkthrough that onboard users through 3D globe navigation, regional screening, horizon analysis, and power budgeting.
  • Transparent Calculations & Scientific Provenance: Every technical term and formula features an interactive [i] card explaining the underlying physics, showing live calculation inputs, and citing the exact NASA technical standard.
  • WCAG-Compliant UI/UX Design: Built in accordance with WCAG accessibility standards featuring high-contrast readability, full keyboard shortcuts, and dual-coded status badges paired with color-vision-deficiency-safe palettes (Okabe-Ito, Viridis) so data is never communicated by color alone.

Our web app also stands on multiple tools that make up its architecture. These include:

  • Languages: TypeScript, JavaScript (ES2022), GLSL (OpenGL Shading Language for Three.js shaders), Python 3, HTML5, CSS3.
    • React 18 for UI architecture and reactive controls.
    • Three.js and React Three Fiber (R3F) for the 3D planetary rendering engine, cube-sphere quadtree, and GPU shadow baking.
    • D3.js (d3-scale, d3-shape) for SVG power curves, cumulative energy graphs, and 360 horizon silhouettes.
    • Zustand for lightweight, high-performance global state management.
    • Astronomy Engine (Don Cross) for Tier-1 local analytical ephemeris (VSOP87 planetary theory, Chapront lunar theory, and IAU WGCCRE lunar libration models with E1 through E13 physical arguments).
    • Brent’s Numerical Root-Finding Algorithm for second-level event boundary precision.
    • Web Workers for multi-threaded background forward search calculations.
    • Vite with an integrated Node.js caching proxy (/api/horizons) to query NASA JPL Horizons and bypass browser CORS limitations.
    • Vitest running a 45-test verification suite covering ephemeris, geometry, and power models.
    • Python (numpy, scipy, pillow, tifffile) with multi-threaded HTTP Range downloading and custom GeoTIFF float-predictor decoding to process ~5 GB of raw NASA datasets into compressed multi-resolution tile pyramids.
  • Hardware/Environment: Runs entirely on standard commercial client hardware inside any modern web browser supporting WebGL 2.0.

We have considered many factors in the making of our Lunar Browser, which include :

  • Extreme Low-Angle Sunlight: Because the Sun barely skims the polar horizon (at roughly 1.5°), shadows stretch for dozens of kilometers. We modeled the physical 0.53° width of the solar disk so partial eclipses and grazing ridge shadows are simulated realistically.
  • Solar Power Generation Requirements: We let users configure panel tilt, azimuth tracking, solar cell efficiency, and dust degradation to model actual battery charge and discharge cycles over time.
  • Earth Libration: From the lunar pole, the Earth wobbles by several degrees over a 27-day cycle. We track this line-of-sight clearance continuously.
  • Slope & Landing Ellipses: We calculate slopes across both rover (5 m) and lander (100 m) baselines, testing whether a 100 m to 500 m landing ellipse has at least 95% safe ground.
  • Data Honesty: High-resolution 5 m maps often contain interpolated data where laser passes missed. We check per-pixel shot counts so unmeasured terrain is never marked safe by accident.

The lunar South Pole is especially important for future NASA missions. Where missions once faced the unknown, HECATE provides data-driven predictions that facilitate decisions for mission planners and helps students understand lunar exploration challenges via an intuitive, real-time 3D decision engine.
